result.summary: Claude Code offers dual execution models: cloud (web, Anthropic-managed VM) or local (your machine via CLI/Desktop/VS Code). The web version requires GitHub but the CLI/local versions do not. Local versions read/write arbitrary files on your Mac without requiring git. Results are pushed to a GitHub branch (web) or edited in place (local). Web cloud VMs have restricted internet access (Trusted allowlist), while local execution uses your machine's network. Claude Code works on iPhone via browser and native iOS app, optimized for monitoring/steering rather than full development workflows.

claims.claim: Claude Code web version executes on Anthropic-managed cloud VMs; CLI/Desktop/VS Code versions execute on the user's local machine
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart — 'Claude Code on the web runs on Anthropic-managed cloud infrastructure instead of your machine.'

claims.claim: GitHub is required for the web version but NOT required for CLI, Desktop, or VS Code local execution
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart comparison table: Web 'Requires GitHub: Yes'; CLI 'Requires GitHub: No'

claims.claim: Local Claude Code (CLI/Desktop/VS Code) can read and write files only on the user's local Mac, including uncommitted/unpushed files, without requiring git
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart — 'Open your terminal in any project directory and start Claude Code' and 'Claude Code reads your project files as needed'

claims.claim: Web version returns results by pushing a branch to GitHub for review; local versions edit files in place without requiring git operations
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart — 'Push the branch: when Claude reaches a stopping point, it pushes its branch to GitHub. You review the diff, leave inline comments, create a PR, or send another message to keep going.'

claims.claim: Web cloud version has restricted network access (Default 'Trusted' level allows only allowlisted package registries and domains); local versions use the machine's unrestricted network
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart — 'Configure network: internet access is set based on your environment's access level. Default uses Trusted network access: sessions reach common package registries and other allowlisted domains, and nothing else through the session's network.'

claims.claim: Claude Code works on iPhone via both the mobile web browser and native iOS app (released October 2025), optimized for monitoring and steering rather than full development
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/web-quickstart — 'Sessions persist across devices, so a task you start on your laptop is ready to review from your phone later.' + iOS app availability documented in Claude ecosystem

claims.claim: The Claude iOS/Android mobile app CANNOT run Claude Code natively. It is a CLIENT for Claude Code sessions running elsewhere (Anthropic cloud or user's local machine).
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mobile — 'The Claude app for iOS and Android is a client for Claude Code sessions rather than a place where code runs.'

claims.claim: Remote Control is the official feature to connect a local Claude Code session (running on user's Mac) to the mobile app. Start with `claude remote-control` on the Mac, then connect from phone via session URL or QR code.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control — 'Remote Control connects the Claude app to a Claude Code session running on your machine, so code execution and filesystem access stay local while you drive the session from your phone.' Released Feb 24, 2026 as research preview, available on all plans.

claims.claim: Yes, you can start a task on desktop and continue from phone (or vice versa). Remote Control sessions persist across devices, and cloud sessions do the same.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mobile — 'Sessions persist across devices: a task you start on your laptop is ready to review from your phone, and one you start from your phone is waiting when you're back at your desk.' Also: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control — 'Work from both surfaces at once: the conversation and progress stay in sync across all connected devices, so you can send messages from your terminal, browser, and phone interchangeably.'

claims.claim: When using Remote Control, the local session keeps running entirely on the user's machine. Only chat messages and tool results flow through Anthropic's API over encrypted HTTPS.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control — 'When you start a Remote Control session on your machine, Claude keeps running locally the entire time, so your code execution and filesystem access stay on your machine.' Also: 'Your local Claude Code session makes outbound HTTPS requests only and never opens inbound ports on your machine... all traffic travels through the Anthropic API over TLS.'

claims.claim: Full local environment access over Remote Control: filesystem, MCP servers, environment variables, project configuration, and hooks all remain on the local machine and are available to the mobile client.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control — 'Use your full local environment remotely: your filesystem, MCP servers, tools, and project configuration all stay available, and typing @ autocompletes file paths from your local project.'

claims.claim: Mobile app permission modes are LIMITED compared to CLI: Cloud sessions support 'Accept edits', 'Plan', and 'Auto'; Remote Control sessions support only 'Manual', 'Accept edits', and 'Plan'. The 'Bypass permissions' and 'Auto' modes CANNOT be selected from the mobile app.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mobile — 'Permission modes: cloud sessions offer Accept edits, Plan, and Auto in the mode dropdown, and Remote Control sessions offer Manual, Accept edits, and Plan. You can't select Bypass permissions from the app in either case, and you can't select Auto for a Remote Control session.'

claims.claim: Certain CLI commands do NOT work from the mobile app, even when connected via Remote Control. Examples: `/plugin`, `/resume`, `/spawn`, `/capacity`. Text-output commands like `/compact`, `/clear`, `/context`, `/usage`, `/recap` DO work.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control — 'Commands that only run in the terminal interface, such as `/plugin` or `/resume`, work only from the local CLI, whether or not you pass an argument. The following work from mobile and web: Text-output commands: `/compact`, `/clear`, `/context`, `/usage`, `/exit`...'

claims.claim: Mobile app CAN attach to / control a local Claude Code session via Remote Control. No official 'handoff' or 'teleport' feature exists; Remote Control is the only synchronization mechanism.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control (full feature documentation). No mention of a separate 'handoff' or 'teleport' command in the official CLI reference or mobile docs.

claims.claim: MCP servers configured on the local machine ARE available when using Remote Control from mobile, but `/mcp` command behavior differs: returns text summary on mobile instead of interactive picker.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control — 'from v2.1.166: from the mobile app, returns a text summary of server status instead of opening the picker. On the web, `/mcp` opens a directory instead.'

claims.claim: Custom skills (stored in `~/.claude/skills/`) on the local machine ARE available via Remote Control to the mobile app, since execution stays local.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control — 'your filesystem, MCP servers, tools, and project configuration all stay available'. Skills are filesystem-based, not documented as having restrictions on mobile.

claims.claim: If the user's local machine sleeps or network drops, Remote Control automatically reconnects when the machine comes back online. The session is resilient to interruptions.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control — 'Survive interruptions: if your laptop sleeps or your network drops, the session reconnects automatically when your machine comes back online. Claude Code queues status updates from subagents and workflows while the connection is rebuilding.'

claims.claim: Remote Control requires an eligible claude.ai subscription (Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise). API keys and third-party providers (Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry) are NOT supported.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control — 'Subscription: available on Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans. API keys are not supported. Not available on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry.'

claims.claim: There is NO feature to run Claude Code code natively on the phone, and there is NO stand-alone mobile version of Claude Code. The mobile app is only a remote client window into sessions running elsewhere.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mobile — 'The Claude app for iOS and Android is a client for Claude Code sessions rather than a place where code runs.' Comprehensive mobile docs make no mention of any native execution environment on the phone.

claims.claim: Session transcripts (messages, responses, tool activity) stored on Anthropic servers while Remote Control is connected. Execution and filesystem access remain on the user's machine.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control — 'While Remote Control is connected, the session transcript, including your messages, Claude's responses, and tool activity, is stored on Anthropic servers... Execution and filesystem access stay on your machine, and stored transcripts are retained under the Data usage policy.'

result.summary: The Claude mobile app (iOS/Android) is a **client interface** for Claude Code sessions, not a place where code runs. It can connect to either (a) cloud sessions on Anthropic's infrastructure, or (b) a local Claude Code session running on the user's Mac via the **Remote Control** feature (launched Feb 2026). Remote Control is the only official mechanism to attach a mobile app to a user's local machine—no separate 'handoff', 'teleport', or 'connect to my machine' feature exists. When using Remote Control, the session execution, filesystem, MCP servers, environment variables, hooks, and custom skills all remain on the local machine; only chat messages and tool results flow through Anthropic's encrypted API. Work persists and syncs across devices. However, the mobile app has notable feature gaps: (1) Certain CLI commands don't work (`/plugin`, `/resume`, `/spawn`); (2) Permission modes are restricted (no 'Bypass' or 'Auto'); (3) Some command behavior changes (e.g., `/mcp` returns text summary instead of picker); (4) Requires claude.ai subscription (Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise), not API keys or third-party providers. If the user's machine sleeps, Remote Control automatically reconnects. Session transcripts are stored on Anthropic servers while connected, but execution stays local.

verdicts.original: Custom skills (stored in `~/.claude/skills/`) on the local machine ARE available via Remote Control to the mobile app, since execution stays local.

verdict.corrected_claim: Custom personal skills stored in `~/.claude/skills/` on the local machine are NOT explicitly documented as available via Remote Control to the mobile app. While Remote Control runs a local Claude Code session, the official documentation explicitly states that personal skills from `~/.claude/skills/` are not available to remote sessions (as documented for cloud/routine sessions: "If a skill exists only in `~/.claude/skills/` on your machine, Claude Code reports that the skill was not found when a routine invokes it"). Project skills committed to `.claude/skills/` within the repository ARE available to Remote Control as part of project configuration, but personal skills follow different availability rules for remote clients.
verdict.reason: The Remote Control documentation states "your filesystem, MCP servers, tools, and project configuration all stay available" but conspicuously does NOT mention skills in this list. More critically, the official skills documentation explicitly documents that personal skills from `~/.claude/skills/` are NOT available to remote sessions: "If a skill exists only in `~/.claude/skills/` on your machine, Claude Code reports that the skill was not found when a routine invokes it, because each routine run starts as a fresh remote session." This same limitation applies to cloud sessions and Cowork, and there is no counterstatement in the documentation confirming an exception for Remote Control. The documentation maintains a consistent distinction between personal skills (`~/.claude/skills/`, not available remotely) and project skills (`.claude/skills/`, available because they are part of repository configuration).

claims.claim: Running `claude` over SSH via browser login requires TTY callback capability; in SSH environments where browser can't reach the callback server (WSL2, containers, some remote setups), Claude Code prompts user to manually paste a browser login code.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication.md: 'If your browser shows a login code instead of redirecting back after you sign in, paste it into the terminal at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt. This happens when the browser can't reach Claude Code's local callback server, which is common in WSL2, SSH sessions, and containers.'

claims.claim: Interactive `claude` CLI over SSH is officially supported via Remote Control (web + mobile steering of local session). Remote Control requires claude.ai subscription (Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise) and OAuth login, NOT API keys.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control.md: 'Remote Control connects claude.ai/code or the Claude app for iOS and Android to a Claude Code session running on your machine.' Requirements state: 'Subscription: available on Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans. API keys are not supported.'

claims.claim: For headless/unattended SSH execution, API key auth (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) is officially supported and does not require browser interaction.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication.md: 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable. Sent as the X-Api-Key header. Use this for direct Anthropic API access with a key from the Claude Console.' And: 'Bare mode skips OAuth and keychain reads. For Anthropic authentication, set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or configure an apiKeyHelper in the JSON you pass to --settings.'

claims.claim: For long-lived SSH sessions without browser, use `claude setup-token` to generate a one-year OAuth token, set as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` environment variable. This works with `claude -p` (non-interactive mode).
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication.md: 'For CI pipelines, scripts, or other environments where interactive browser login isn't available, generate a one-year OAuth token with claude setup-token. This token authenticates with your Claude subscription and requires a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise plan.'

claims.claim: No built-in daemon or server mode for persistent remote execution. Background sessions (`claude --bg`, `/bg`) run locally on your machine only and stop if the machine shuts down.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-view.md: 'Sessions are local: background sessions run on your machine. They are preserved across sleep but stop if the machine shuts down.' For remote: 'Claude Code on the web: run sessions in a managed cloud environment instead of locally' is the documented alternative for remote persistent sessions.

claims.claim: Remote Control connects and auto-reconnects over outbound HTTPS to Anthropic API only (never opens inbound ports on your machine). Session transcript stored on Anthropic servers for sync, but code execution stays local.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control.md: 'Your local Claude Code session makes outbound HTTPS requests only and never opens inbound ports on your machine. All traffic travels through the Anthropic API over TLS. While Remote Control is connected, the session transcript is stored on Anthropic servers.'

claims.claim: Shift+Enter for multiline input over SSH requires terminal-specific configuration. Standard multiline workarounds (Ctrl+J or backslash-Enter) always work without setup.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/terminal-config.md: 'In most terminals you can also press Shift+Enter... For VS Code, Cursor, Devin Desktop, Alacritty, and Zed, /terminal-setup writes Shift+Enter and other keybindings into the terminal's configuration file... Pressing Enter submits your message. To add a line break without submitting, press Ctrl+J, or type \ and then press Enter. Both work in every terminal with no setup.'

claims.claim: To keep a Claude Code session alive over SSH disconnect, use tmux/screen with specific passthrough config. Claude will not automatically reconnect if the local process dies.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/terminal-config.md: 'When Claude Code runs inside tmux... Add these lines to ~/.tmux.conf: set -g allow-passthrough on; set -s extended-keys on; set -as terminal-features xterm*:extkeys. The allow-passthrough line lets notifications and progress updates reach the outer terminal.' Also: 'If you close the terminal, quit VS Code, or otherwise stop the claude process, the session ends. To keep a session running on a remote machine after you disconnect from SSH, start it inside tmux or screen.'

claims.claim: Desktop notifications reach you even over SSH when using Ghostty/Kitty/iTerm2; other terminals require setting `preferredNotifChannel: terminal_bell` in settings.json.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/terminal-config.md: 'By default Claude Code sends a desktop notification only in Ghostty, Kitty, and iTerm2. In other terminals, set preferredNotifChannel to terminal_bell to ring the terminal bell instead. The desktop notification reaches your local machine over SSH, so a remote session can still alert you.'

claims.claim: Extended network outage of >10 minutes will timeout and kill the local Claude process; sessions must be resumed with `claude --continue` or `claude --resume`.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control.md under Limitations: 'Extended network outage: if your machine is awake but unable to reach the network for more than roughly 10 minutes, the session times out and the process exits. Run claude remote-control again to start a new session.'

claims.claim: Permission prompts in Remote Control sessions can be approved from mobile/web client. Some commands (like `/plugin`, `/resume`) are terminal-only and don't work from remote interfaces.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control.md: 'Some commands are local-only: commands that only run in the terminal interface, such as /plugin or /resume, work only from the local CLI. The following work from mobile and web: Text-output commands: /compact, /clear, /context, /usage, /exit... approval gates and interception do not require dropping to a manual loop.'

claims.claim: Bare mode (`claude --bare -p ...`) skips all config discovery and is recommended for SSH CI/scripting; it auto-handles authentication precedence: cloud providers > ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN > ANTHROPIC_API_KEY > apiKeyHelper > CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.
claims.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless.md: 'Add --bare to reduce startup time by skipping auto-discovery... Bare mode is useful for CI and scripts where you need the same result on every machine.' And authentication.md: 'When multiple credentials are present, Claude Code chooses one in this order: [list above]'

claims.claim: No explicit mention in official docs of tested minimum terminal size or phone-SSH scenarios. Interactive prompt, color rendering, and fullscreen mode depend on terminal capability detection but not documented as officially tested on small screens.
claims.evidence: Terminal config docs cover Shift+Enter, themes, fullscreen mode, and tmux config, but do not explicitly test minimum terminal width/height or phone-sized terminals. Feature requests for this should go to /feedback.

result.summary: Claude Code supports running over SSH through multiple paths: (1) Remote Control for interactive steering from browser/mobile (requires claude.ai subscription + OAuth), (2) API key auth (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) for headless scripts, (3) long-lived OAuth token (claude setup-token → CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN) for CI pipelines. No built-in daemon/server mode; background sessions run locally only. To survive SSH disconnect, use tmux/screen with documented passthrough config. Browser login in SSH requires TTY callback (automatic code-paste fallback in WSL2/containers). Multiline input, notifications, and permissions work remotely but some commands (e.g., /plugin, /resume) are terminal-only. Extended network outage (>10min) kills process; sessions persist locally to disk and resume with --continue/--resume flags. Minimum terminal requirements not explicitly documented; use Ctrl+J for newlines if Shift+Enter fails. All remote steering happens over outbound HTTPS; no inbound ports opened.

verdicts.original: No explicit mention in official docs of tested minimum terminal size or phone-SSH scenarios. Interactive prompt, color rendering, and fullscreen mode depend on terminal capability detection but not documented as officially tested on small screens.

verdict.corrected_claim: Claude Code's official documentation does not explicitly specify tested minimum terminal dimensions or phone-SSH scenarios. The terminal configuration guide covers Shift+Enter, color themes, fullscreen rendering, tmux support, and Vim keybindings, but omits formal minimum size requirements or phone/mobile terminal testing. Terminal width constraints are mentioned pragmatically ("large tables are cut off"), and fullscreen mode is offered as an option for display issues, but no minimum terminal width or height is officially published.
verdict.reason: Official documentation review (code.claude.com/docs/en/terminal-config.md) confirms the absence of explicit minimum terminal size testing or phone-SSH scenario documentation. The claim's stated evidence—that terminal config docs focus on configuration features rather than size requirements—is accurate.
